status_summary: Several Section 232 actions address the named sectors, but they are tariff and negotiation tools that cover all source countries and do not eliminate dependence on China. Proclamation 11002 (signed 2026-01-14) set a 25 percent duty on certain advanced computing chips with broad exemptions, and Proclamation 11001 of the same date on processed critical minerals directed negotiations and left import restrictions as a later option. Proclamation 11020 (signed 2026-04-02) set a 100 percent duty on imported patented pharmaceuticals, effective 2026-07-31 for listed companies and 2026-09-29 for others, with reduced or zero rates for companies with onshoring plans or pricing agreements and for certain partners, and exempted generics for now. On 2026-02-02 EXIM approved a loan of up to $10 billion for Project Vault, a public-private strategic critical minerals reserve. None of the proclamations names China. In an arrangement reported 2025-11-01, China agreed to suspend its October 2025 rare earth export controls for one year and issue general licenses, which relies on continued Chinese supply rather than reducing it.
